answer: A haven is not a hiding place; it is a bonded escrow. Every identity must post a bond sized by how many cluster members already share its canyon, so the k-th claim in a canyon costs k squared and a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated witnesses. Bonds settle in copper, are held for several epochs, and cannot be pooled, lent or reassigned, so one backer cannot cover many heads. A random audit replays a claim and voids the whole canyon when the witness cannot confirm the work, which makes purchased silence worthless.
